To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fluid oscillations that are often called buffet and that occur for flow past airfoils and wings at sufficiently large angles-of-attack are analogous to the von Karman vortex shedding that is well known for bluff bodies in cross flow.

the flow oscillation frequencies for a bluff body in a cross-flow (von Karman vortex street) are the same as the oscillation frequencies for the buffet that occurs at high angles of attack for an airfoil in transonic flow.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the aerodynamic response of an airfoil to a buffet-like excitation.
the aerodynamic response of a bluff body (a circular cylinder or an airfoil) in cross flow.

the aerodynamic response of an oscillating airfoil in transonic buffeting flow, with particular attention to the effect of angle of attack and the effect of the amplitude of oscillation on the amplitude of the oscillatory response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a large-amplitude airfoil oscillation at or near the natural frequency of the flow oscillation, i.e., the buffet frequency, can lead to an increase in the amplitude of the oscillating airfoil.
the airfoil oscillates at the buffet frequency and the amplitude is determined by the static angle of attack and the oscillation amplitude.

the flow oscillations induced by an oscillating airfoil in transonic flow are not simply due to the von Karman vortex shedding, but that the flow oscillation is a complex interaction between vortex shedding and the flow oscillation induced by the oscillating airfoil.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the buffet phenomenon in transonic flow is analogous to the von Karman vortex-street phenomenon in subsonic flow, with the same reduced frequency and Strouhal number.
the flow oscillations for bluff-body flow are indeed similar to the buffet oscillations for airfoils in high angle-of-attack flow.

we have demonstrated the feasibility of using the bluff body in cross-flow as a model for the flow over an airfoil at large angles of attack, with the added benefit of the ability to vary the Strouhal number or reduced frequency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the flow around an airfoil in transonic buffet is similar to the flow around a cylinder in cross flow, with the Strouhal number being the same in both cases.
the buffet frequency is a function of angle of attack.
, in the case of the airfoil at high angles of attack, the buffet and von Karman vortex streets are not the same phenomenon.
